input.rationale: The read-index ack thread is now fully evidenced (measured holds with a retained receipt and a refuted defect claim), so I reselected onto the one in-model consequence of the same v3.7.0 rewrite that I earlier left unclaimed: readOnly.addRequest no longer deduplicates by request context, and every admitted MsgReadIndex also triggers a heartbeat broadcast, so the documented retry contract interacts with a queue and an ack map that have no bound. I record it as a new sourced investigation with an explicit predicate, a behavior fact, and an open necessary question instead of asserting a defect, because whether it is reportable depends on how the caller is permitted to retry and on the leader's quorum situation, and I have not measured either.

investigations.question: Can a caller that follows the documented ReadIndex retry contract grow the leader's per-request read state without bound? Specifically: does each retried MsgReadIndex (same RequestCtx) add one unconfirmedReads entry and one heartbeat broadcast that are never collapsed, and is there any in-model state (leader isolated from a quorum, checkQuorum disabled or not yet fired) under which the entries are never confirmed and never dropped?
investigations.hypothesis: readOnly.addRequest appends unconditionally, without the context-keyed deduplication the v3.6.0 implementation performed, and sendMsgReadIndexResponse calls bcastHeartbeat for every admitted request. Entries leave unconfirmedReads only when a quorum acks the recorded position (readOnly.maybeAdvance), so a leader that cannot obtain quorum acks retains every retried request and rebroadcasts for each, which grows memory and generated traffic with the number of caller retries rather than with the number of distinct reads.
investigations.discriminator: Establish whether the retry contract permits an unbounded number of retries with an identical RequestCtx while the leader stays in StateLeader without quorum confirmation (checkQuorum disabled, or the retry rate exceeding the election timeout). If that state is reachable under permitted use, the growth is an in-model bounded-resource concern; if the caller is required to bound retries or the leader always confirms or steps down first, the behavior is benign and the suspicion is refuted.

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlySafe admission and growth, in this snapshot: every MsgReadIndex that reaches a leader is admitted individually - if the cluster is not a singleton and committedEntryInCurrentTerm() holds, sendMsgReadIndexResponse adds one entry to readOnly.unconfirmedReads via readOnly.addRequest (which appends without any lookup of an existing request with the same context) and then broadcasts a heartbeat carrying heartbeatCtx(); if committedEntryInCurrentTerm() does not hold, the raw message is appended to pendingReadIndexMessages and released (one response per queued message) only later, each release again going through addRequest plus a heartbeat broadcast. Entries are removed from unconfirmedReads only by readOnly.maybeAdvance, which requires the quorum ack position to exceed confirmedReads. Nothing in the admission path inspects the RequestCtx, so N retries with an identical context produce N unconfirmedReads entries and N heartbeat broadcasts.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe, leader in StateLeader. The behavior is a property of admission, independent of whether the reads are eventually confirmed; under a healthy quorum each retry is confirmed quickly, so the queue stays short. The node-level contract that makes retries the caller's duty is stated at node.go:222-223 ('request can be lost without notice, therefore it is user's job to ensure read index retries').

gaps.question: What bounds (if any) the number of outstanding read requests a client may have with the same RequestCtx while a leader is in StateLeader but unable to obtain quorum acknowledgements - is any bound stated by the ReadIndex contract, by etcd's usage, or enforced by the library (and does checkQuorum guarantee the leader steps down before the state persists)?

interpretations.rationale: Source-only account; no execution is claimed and none was run for this predicate. What the sources establish: the admission path is per request and context-blind (read_only.go addRequest appends; raft.go sendMsgReadIndexResponse admits then broadcasts; bcastHeartbeat uses heartbeatCtx derived from confirmedReads plus len(unconfirmedReads)), removal requires a quorum ack position to advance maybeAdvance, and the node contract explicitly tells callers to retry ReadIndex requests that can be lost. The predicate I am testing - a caller following that contract can grow the leader's read state without bound - therefore holds mechanically for the admission half, and I demonstrated the arithmetic of the same structures directly with the retained experiment (ack positions and the slice bound depend on confirmedReads and len(unconfirmedReads)). What I cannot settle from sources alone is the applicability half: whether a permitted caller may keep retrying while the leader remains in StateLeader without quorum confirmation, or whether checkQuorum guarantees step-down before that state persists, or whether the library/downstream usage sets a retry bound. I deliberately did not convert this into an asserted defect: (a) the scenario requires the caller to retry without bound - a client that retries forever is the party repeatedly re-creating its own obligation, and the contract says retries are its job without specifying a bound; (b) a leader that cannot obtain quorum acks must not confirm reads, so the nonprogress itself is correct behavior, and only the unbounded accumulation and per-retry broadcast are at issue; (c) with a healthy quorum each retry is confirmed on the next heartbeat response, so the queue length is bounded by the round-trip, and I have not observed a case where it is not; (d) the v3.7.0 changelog presents the removal of context-keyed handling as the fix for stale read indexes on retries, so treating the new growth behavior as a defect would need a bounded-consequence argument I do not yet have. The gap above records exactly what would decide it. This is independent of the refuted ack-validation thread: that one concerned an out-of-contract Context, this one concerns in-contract repeated admission.

knowledge.assertion: each admitted MsgReadIndex appends one unconfirmedReads entry and broadcasts a heartbeat, with no context-keyed deduplication

limitations: Source-only and unresolved: no execution measured unconfirmedReads growth under repeated same-context retries, and no downstream usage (etcd) was examined, so the practical bound is unknown.
The account assumes ReadOnlySafe; lease-based reads never enter the ack/queue structures.
Severity is unassessed: I have not shown a concrete memory figure, a triggered OOM, or a liveness failure, only the absence of an internal bound.

investigations.question: In the ReadOnlySafe read-index flow, is a heartbeat response's Context validated against the outstanding read requests before it is used to confirm a read index, and what bounds the value used to slice unconfirmedReads?
investigations.hypothesis: Refined after resolving the gap: readOnly.recvAck does store a peer-supplied Context as a raw read-position ack with no check that the leader emitted it, and maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads by the resulting quorum position without clamping. But every legal producer in this snapshot echoes a value the live leader's heartbeatCtx produced (handleHeartbeat is the sole writer of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context), the readOnly instance is created only by raft.reset at a leadership transition, and the emitted position equals a message total that is non-decreasing, so the quorum position can never exceed confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads) in-model. The two consequences (slice-bounds panic; confirming a read no quorum observed) require a Context outside the set heartbeatCtx emitted, which no in-model producer supplies.
investigations.discriminator: Resolved: enumerate the sites that create the readOnly instance (only raft.reset, called from becomeFollower/becomeCandidate/becomeLeader) and the writers of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context (only handleHeartbeat, echoing m.Context). investigations.question: When a MsgReadIndex is postponed because the leader has not committed an entry in its term, is that queued duty eventually completed with a read index at least as large as the one the same request would have received at admission, including when the queue survives loss and later reacquisition of leadership (and when the node is deposed, removed, or restarted in between)?
investigations.hypothesis: The queue is not cleared by raft.reset (term or state change), so a request admitted at term T is released later, while the node is leader again at term T' > T. Release recomputes the index from the live r.raftLog.committed, and every write to raftLog.committed is non-decreasing (commitTo refuses to lower it; loadState and log restore are guarded to only raise it above the current value). The completed read index is therefore >= the committed index at admission, so the surviving duty cannot produce a stale read index.
investigations.discriminator: Look for any site that lowers raftLog.committed after a request is queued, or any release path that reuses an index captured before admission instead of reading the live commit index. None would mean the stale-index suspicion is defeated; a lowering site or a cached-index release would revive it. Secondary: whether the queue can be released while the node is not the current leader (releasePendingReadIndexMessages is only called from the leader's MsgAppResp path and re-checks committedEntryInCurrentTerm).

investigations.question: Once a leader puts a follower's Progress into StateSnapshot, which actors can restore replication to that follower, and is there an enabled repair when the follower applied the snapshot but the corresponding MsgAppResp is lost?

knowledge.statement: For ReadOnlySafe, the leader confirms reads as follows: sendMsgReadIndexResponse calls readOnly.addRequest(committed, m), self-acks by recvAck(r.id, heartbeatCtx()) and broadcasts a heartbeat carrying heartbeatCtx(); heartbeatCtx encodes confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads) in 8 little-endian bytes; on each MsgHeartbeatResp with non-empty Context the leader calls readOnly.recvAck(m.From, m.Context), which stores max(existing, binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(Context)) in acks[m.From]; maybeAdvance computes newConfirmedReads = quorum.JointConfig.CommittedIndex(ro) over acks (unacked voters count as 0), and if newConfirmedReads > confirmedReads it returns unconfirmedReads[:newConfirmedReads-confirmedReads] and advances confirmedReads. No comparison is made between the received Context and any value the leader emitted.
knowledge.conditions: Leader in StateLeader with ReadOnlySafe; the ack map and unconfirmedReads are per readOnly instance, recreated by raft.reset on each state/term change. Values in acks are positions (counts of admitted read requests), not log indexes.

knowledge.statement: Under the framework's own producers, every value written into readOnly.acks equals a value heartbeatCtx produced for this readOnly lifetime, and heartbeatCtx values are non-decreasing and at most the number of admitted read requests. Therefore for a faithful cluster the quorum position newConfirmedReads never exceeds confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads); the slicing in maybeAdvance is in range and each confirmed read corresponds to a heartbeat sent after that read was admitted.
knowledge.conditions: All peers echo MsgHeartbeatResp.Context exactly as produced by the leader's heartbeatCtx (the only context the checked-in follower path writes, via handleHeartbeat), and the leader's readOnly is not recreated between request admission and response handling except across state/term changes, after which lower-term responses are ignored by raft.Step.

knowledge.statement: In this snapshot the ReadOnlySafe ack bookkeeping is in-model consistent: (1) r.readOnly is reassigned only in raft.reset (:809) and reset is called only by becomeFollower (:893), becomeCandidate (:908, term+1) and becomeLeader (:939, the candidate's term), so a readOnly instance is live only while its node is leader at one term; (2) raft.Step drops a lower-term MsgHeartbeatResp before dispatch (:1158-1175); (3) the only producer of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context is handleHeartbeat (:1837), echoing the leader's heartbeat Context, and vote contexts are sent on MsgVote (:1071); (4) heartbeatCtx emits exactly confirmedReads+len(unconfirmedReads), which addRequest only grows and maybeAdvance preserves. Therefore every value in readOnly.acks is at most the current message total, newConfirmedReads-confirmedReads can never exceed len(unconfirmedReads), and each returned read corresponds to a heartbeat emitted after that request was admitted and acknowledged by a quorum. The slice-bounds panic and premature confirmation observed when a probe supplied an out-of-contract Context are not reachable through the library's own producers.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; leadership terms strictly increase (becomeCandidate panics from StateLeader and increments the term); cluster members run this library's follower path (including a v3.6.0 node, which also echoes m.Context); no two leaders exist in the same term. Excludes a peer or intermediary that fabricates or corrupts MsgHeartbeatResp.Context, which is outside the crash-fault model.

knowledge.statement: pendingReadIndexMessages lifecycle for MsgReadIndex on a leader: in stepLeader (:1355-1372) a request is answered immediately when the cluster is a singleton or when committedEntryInCurrentTerm() holds, and is otherwise appended to r.pendingReadIndexMessages without a term stamp; raft.reset (:781-812) does not clear the slice, so it survives step-downs, re-elections and being removed from the config; releasePendingReadIndexMessages (:2127-2144) is invoked only from the leader's MsgAppResp fast path after maybeCommit() returns true (:1546-1556), returns early with an error log if committedEntryInCurrentTerm() no longer holds, and otherwise swaps the slice out and passes each stored message to sendMsgReadIndexResponse, which captures the index as r.raftLog.committed at that moment (ReadOnlySafe also re-enters the addRequest/heartbeat confirmation flow for it).
knowledge.conditions: Node acts as leader; r.raftLog.committed is the only source of the read index. Commit index monotonicity holds because commitTo (:322-330) assigns only when l.committed < tocommit, log restore is reached only when the snapshot index exceeds the current committed (log.go :463-470 guard), and loadState (:2037-2047) rejects any state.commit below the current committed.

knowledge.statement: Leader-side StateSnapshot handling: maybeSendSnapshot (:666-694) refuses to send while pr.RecentActive is false, and otherwise calls pr.BecomeSnapshot(snapshotIndex) which sets State=StateSnapshot, PendingSnapshot=Next-1 and pauses the follower. While in that state Progress.IsPaused() returns true unconditionally (tracker/progress.go :262-282), so maybeSendAppend returns immediately, bcastAppend is a no-op for that peer, and the MsgHeartbeatResp branch's sendAppend (:1588-1596) also sends nothing. Exactly two producers can leave the state: (1) stepLeader's MsgAppResp handler (:1518-1546) when pr.MaybeUpdate(m.GetIndex()) is true (m.Index strictly greater than pr.Match) and then pr.Match+1 >= raftLog.firstIndex(), which runs BecomeProbe followed by BecomeReplicate; and (2) stepLeader's MsgSnapStatus handler (:1612-1634) from the application's ReportSnapshot, which returns early unless pr.State == StateSnapshot, then clears PendingSnapshot when the snapshot failed and calls BecomeProbe either way.
knowledge.conditions: Node is leader; the peer is a tracked follower or learner. The follower emits the MsgAppResp either by applying the snapshot (handleSnapshot sends MsgAppResp with its last index) or by ignoring an obsolete snapshot (handleSnapshot sends MsgAppResp with its committed index). ReportSnapshot reaches the leader as MsgSnapStatus only when the application calls it.

knowledge.statement: When readOnly.recvAck is given an 8-byte Context value larger than the number of outstanding read requests, the ReadOnlySafe confirmation path behaves as follows in this snapshot. With a quorum of such values (leader self-ack position 1 plus two peers at position 2^40, voters {1,2,3}), readOnly.maybeAdvance panics inside its slice expression: 'runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:1099511627776] with capacity 1'. With a single such value (two admitted reads, leader self-ack position 2, an honest peer at position 1, one peer at position 2 that received no heartbeat carrying position 2), maybeAdvance does not panic and instead returns both admitted reads (advanced=2, confirmed_reads=2), i.e. it confirms a read index that the forged voter never observed. Both outcomes were observed with the ack map, unconfirmedReads and confirmedReads driven directly; no raft instance, network or storage was involved.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; ack values are injected directly into the unexported readOnly via recvAck instead of being produced by the library's follower path (handleHeartbeat), which is the out-of-contract premise. Quorum position is the median of stored acks because CommittedIndex is evaluated over quorum.JointConfig{1,2,3},nil. Does not apply to ReadOnlyLeaseBased, which does not use the ack map.

interpretations.rationale: Source account (no retained execution). The checked-in ReadOnlySafe flow stores a peer-supplied Context byte string as a read-position ack without any equality check against the positions the leader emitted (read_only.go recvAck/AckedIndex), then derives a quorum position from those stored values and slices unconfirmedReads by it (read_only.go maybeAdvance via quorum.CommittedIndex). A focused local probe on the unexported readOnly, run only as native feedback and not retained as a receipt, reproduced two mechanical consequences when acks carry a value the leader never emitted: (a) three voters with two over-large ack values produced a panic 'slice bounds out of range [:1099511627776] with capacity 1', because newConfirmedReads-confirmedReads exceeded len(unconfirmedReads); (b) with two admitted reads, a single over-large ack combined with the leader's own self-ack reached a 2-of-3 quorum position and confirmed the second read even though that voter had received no heartbeat carrying it, i.e. the response that justifies the read index was not actually observed by a quorum. Both consequences require a Context value outside the set heartbeatCtx emits. Within the crash-fault model the checked-in producers only echo the leader's context (handleHeartbeat copies m.Context; lower-term responses are dropped by raft.Step), so the fact @K_read_pos holds for faithful participants and I have not established an in-model trigger; the v3.6.0 contrast (recvAck keyed acks by exact pending request context and ignored unknown contexts) shows the validation is a deliberate-or-incidental regression of the rewrite rather than a pre-existing property, but a historical comparison is not by itself evidence about reachability here. Counterevidence/limits: (1) the premise is a Context the leader never issued, which is a fault-model violation unless a legal producer exists - this is exactly the open gap; (2) the probe drove readOnly directly, supplying read messages, so it demonstrates the predicate mechanically and not a network path; (3) no retained receipt was produced, so no execution indices are cited. Related in-model pressure noted but not promoted to a claim: addRequest no longer deduplicates by request context, so the same documented retry pattern ('user's job to ensure read index retries') appends one unconfirmed entry and broadcasts one heartbeat per retry for as long as the leader cannot reach quorum confirmation. Because applicability hinges on the missing producer rather than on reproducing the symptom, the defect judgment stays unresolved and the gap above records what would settle it.

interpretations.rationale: Revision of the earlier conditional account for investigation 71f53a32a0c74532a55ad33bc1e71086-question-0. What changed: I answered the recorded necessary gap (71f53a32a0c74532a55ad33bc1e71086-gap-0) by enumerating the two source facts the suspicion depended on - where the readOnly instance is created and who can write MsgHeartbeatResp.Context. r.readOnly is reassigned only at raft.go:809 within raft.reset, and reset is called only from becomeFollower (:893), becomeCandidate (:908) and becomeLeader (:939); handleHeartbeat (:1837) is the sole writer of the heartbeat Context, copying the leader's value, while vote contexts travel on MsgVote (:1071); and raft.Step drops lower-term messages before dispatch (:1158-1175). Hence in-model every stored ack is at most that total, the slice in maybeAdvance is always in range, and each confirmed read was observed by a quorum - the premise of the original suspicion does not hold. Still-applicable findings retained from the prior revision: the observation that recvAck performs no equality check against the emitted contexts and maybeAdvance does not clamp the slice is accurate as a description of the code (knowledge entries 71f53a32a0c74532a55ad33bc1e71086-knowledge-0 and -1 remain valid), and my focused local probe (native feedback, not a retained receipt) did reproduce both a slice-bounds panic and premature confirmation when values outside the emitted set were supplied. What that probe establishes is the code's behavior under an out-of-contract input, not an in-model trigger. Naming the boundary explicitly instead of keeping the claim: within the crash-fault model this is not a safety or liveness defect; the residual property is that a peer or intermediary fabricating or corrupting MsgHeartbeatResp.Context can panic the leader (slice bounds out of range) or advance a read index its peer never justified, which is robustness against a fault class the CFT model excludes. I therefore record it as a scoped fact (@K_read_ack_scope) rather than a defect, and I have no remaining doubt about the question as asked. Independent uncertainty I did not promote to a claim: addRequest no longer deduplicates by request context, so repeated documented ReadIndex retries with the same context accumulate one unconfirmed entry and one heartbeat broadcast per retry while the leader cannot reach a quorum ack; whether that is a reportable bounded-resource concern depends on client retry discipline and is not asserted here.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only account, no retained execution (native feedback only when it could change the reading). Predicate under test: does a postponed MsgReadIndex ever get completed with a read index below its admission-time committed index after surviving an authority transition? Admission: stepLeader queues the message whenever committedEntryInCurrentTerm() is false (:1355-1372); the message carries no index and no term, so nothing about admission is cached. Survival: raft.reset (:781-812) reassigns readOnly and clears votes, progress, pendingConfIndex and uncommittedSize but never touches pendingReadIndexMessages, so the slice persists across step-down, re-election and removal; the deferral is therefore a real queued duty that outlives the leadership under which it was accepted. Completion: releasePendingReadIndexMessages is reached only from the leader's MsgAppResp path where maybeCommit() returned true (:1546-1556) and re-checks committedEntryInCurrentTerm() before acting, so release happens under current leadership in the current term; the index passed to sendMsgReadIndexResponse is r.raftLog.committed read at that moment, not a value captured earlier. Monotonicity: commitTo only assigns when l.committed < tocommit (log.go :322-330); log restore is reached only after the guard that the snapshot index exceeds the current committed (log.go :463-470); loadState panics unless state.commit is >= committed and <= lastIndex (raft.go :2037-2047); maybeAppend commits min(upstream commit, lastnewi). Hence committed never decreases across the serialized event sequence, release is strictly later than admission, and the completed index is >= the admission-time index. The suspicion of a stale read index from a surviving queue is therefore defeated in-model. Retained and still relevant: (a) the queue is deliberately not cleared, so a request queued under a term whose successor leadership never commits in term leaves the duty pending until the client's documented retry; (b) the release path is the only completion producer, so if the node never leads again the duty is never completed by this node - this matches the documented contract that ReadIndex requests can be lost and are the caller's retry responsibility, so it is a contract property rather than a defect; (c) this is a source-only conclusion, so a later retained execution would be needed to turn it into an observation. Independent uncertainty not promoted to a claim: because release recomputes the index, a request postponed under an earlier term can be answered with an index above what it needed, which is safe for linearizability but means the answered index does not identify the request's original position.

knowledge.assertion: the postponed read duty survives reset and is released with a freshly read, monotonically non-decreasing commit index

limitations: Source-only refutation: no retained receipt exercises the queue-survives-term-change path; the argument rests on the listed guard sites being exhaustive for writes to raftLog.committed.

The monotonicity argument is stated under the library's normal serialized Step/Ready execution; it says nothing about an application that mutates Storage or HardState out of band, which is outside the target's responsibility.

interpretations.rationale: Predicate: under the library's stated contract, a follower placed in StateSnapshot has an enabled repair. Source account only. Evidence for the predicate: the library provides one peer-driven repair (a MsgAppResp that strictly advances pr.Match while pr.Match+1 >= firstIndex triggers BecomeProbe/BecomeReplicate) and one explicitly documented application-driven repair (ReportSnapshot, delivered as MsgSnapStatus, which is accepted only while pr.State == StateSnapshot and then clears PendingSnapshot on failure and becomes a probe). The Progress comment at tracker/progress.go :64-84 states this design intent, including that the application must report snapshot failure so the leader resumes probing, and node.go's ReportSnapshot documentation makes that an explicit application duty. I checked for a self-repair path: heartbeats to a paused follower produce MsgHeartbeatResp, but the heartbeat handler's sendAppend is a no-op because IsPaused is true in StateSnapshot, and no timer exits the state; so the library alone does not repair a lost MsgAppResp. That is a responsibility boundary rather than a defect: the local duty (resume replication once either event arrives) is implemented and reachable, and the external event is owed by the application under the documented contract. Boundaries and counterevidence: (a) the trace is source-only with no retained receipt; (b) if an application enabled snapshots but never called ReportSnapshot, a follower whose snapshot response was lost would stay paused, which is a contract violation by the caller, not a target defect; (c) handleSnapshot's ignored-snapshot branch replies with r.raftLog.committed, whose value can be at or below pr.Match, in which case MaybeUpdate is false and that particular MsgAppResp does not repair - the report path remains the required mechanism, consistent with the Progress comment. No comparison is made between the received Context and any value the leader emitted.
knowledge.conditions: Leader in StateLeader with ReadOnlySafe; the ack map and unconfirmedReads are per readOnly instance, recreated by raft.reset on each state/term change. Values in acks are positions (counts of admitted read requests), not log indexes.

knowledge.statement: Under the framework's own producers, every value written into readOnly.acks equals a value heartbeatCtx produced for this readOnly lifetime, and heartbeatCtx values are non-decreasing and at most the number of admitted read requests. knowledge.conditions: All peers echo MsgHeartbeatResp.Context exactly as produced by the leader's heartbeatCtx (the only context the checked-in follower path writes, via handleHeartbeat), and the leader's readOnly is not recreated between request admission and response handling except across state/term changes, after which lower-term responses are ignored by raft.Step.

knowledge.statement: pendingReadIndexMessages lifecycle for MsgReadIndex on a leader: in stepLeader (:1355-1372) a request is answered immediately when the cluster is a singleton or when committedEntryInCurrentTerm() holds, and is otherwise appended to r.pendingReadIndexMessages without a term stamp; raft.reset (:781-812) does not clear the slice, so it survives step-downs, re-elections and being removed from the config; releasePendingReadIndexMessages (:2127-2144) is invoked only from the leader's MsgAppResp fast path after maybeCommit() returns true (:1546-1556), returns early with an error log if committedEntryInCurrentTerm() no longer holds, and otherwise swaps the slice out and passes each stored message to sendMsgReadIndexResponse, which captures the index as r.raftLog.committed at that moment (ReadOnlySafe also re-enters the addRequest/heartbeat confirmation flow for it).

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlySafe admission and growth, in this snapshot: every MsgReadIndex that reaches a leader is admitted individually - if the cluster is not a singleton and committedEntryInCurrentTerm() holds, sendMsgReadIndexResponse adds one entry to readOnly.unconfirmedReads via readOnly.addRequest (which appends without any lookup of an existing request with the same context) and then broadcasts a heartbeat carrying heartbeatCtx(); if committedEntryInCurrentTerm() does not hold, the raw message is appended to pendingReadIndexMessages and released (one response per queued message) only later, each release again going through addRequest plus a heartbeat broadcast. The suspicion of a stale read index from a surviving queue is therefore defeated in-model. Retained and still relevant: (a) the queue is deliberately not cleared, so a request queued under a term whose successor leadership never commits in term leaves the duty pending until the client's documented retry; (b) the release path is the only completion producer, so if the node never leads again the duty is never completed by this node - this matches the documented contract that ReadIndex requests can be lost and are the caller's retry responsibility, so it is a contract property rather than a defect; (c) this is a source-only conclusion, so a later retained execution would be needed to turn it into an observation.
